src.q: Drug-induced enterocolitis syndrome (DIES) has been reported mainly in children receiving amoxicillin/clavulanic acid
There have been severe cases including progression to shock.

src.q: During the administration of high doses of amoxicillin, it is advisable to maintain adequate fluid intake and urinary output in order to reduce the possibility of amoxicillin crystalluria.

rules.action: BUMPS: can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor (differs in emphasis from the SmPC).
rules.sourceWording: can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor

src.q: Amoxicillin, co-amoxiclav, and penicillin V can be taken in pregnancy if recommended by a doctor.

rules.consequence: Both substances pass into milk; infant diarrhoea, fungal infection, sensitisation possible.
rules.action: Use only after benefit/risk assessment.
rules.sourceWording: should only be used during breast-feeding after benefit/risk assessment

src.q: Amoxicillin/clavulanic acid should only be used during breast-feeding after benefit/risk assessment by the physician in charge.

rules.consequence: Negligible milk levels expected; no concerns identified for combinations.
rules.action: Can be used with precautionary infant monitoring (GI upset, oral thrush, rash/breathing problems).
rules.sourceWording: can be used during breastfeeding with precautionary infant monitoring

src.q: All penicillin antibiotics can be used during breastfeeding with precautionary infant monitoring.
Although there is no information on how much passes into breastmilk, studies have not identified any concerns for their use in breastfeeding.

rules.consequence: Increased INR / prolonged prothrombin time reported.
rules.action: Carefully monitor prothrombin time/INR when co-amoxiclav is added or withdrawn; anticoagulant dose may need adjustment.
rules.sourceWording: should be carefully monitored

src.q: If co-administration is necessary, the prothrombin time or international normalised ratio should be carefully monitored with the addition or withdrawal of amoxicillin.
Adjustments in the dose of oral anticoagulants may be necessary to maintain the desired level of anticoagulation

rules.consequence: Penicillins may reduce methotrexate excretion, increasing toxicity.
rules.action: SPS: for short courses (up to 10 days) consider using with caution and monitor for methotrexate toxicity (sore throat, bruising, bleeding).
rules.sourceWording: consider using with caution and advise to monitor for signs of toxicity

src.q: Penicillins may reduce the excretion of methotrexate causing a potential increase in toxicity.
If the duration of penicillin is short (up to 10 days), consider using with caution and advise to monitor for signs of toxicity.

rules.consequence: Allergic skin reactions are more likely.
rules.action: Be aware (no specific action stated).
rules.sourceWording: can increase the likelihood of allergic skin reactions

src.q: Concomitant use of allopurinol during treatment with amoxicillin can increase the likelihood of allergic skin reactions.

rules.consequence: Antibiotic-associated colitis can occur; anti-peristaltic medicines are contraindicated in that situation.
rules.action: If colitis is suspected (severe or persistent diarrhoea): stop co-amoxiclav, consult a physician, and do not give loperamide or other anti-peristaltic medicines.
rules.sourceWording: Anti-peristaltic medicinal products are contraindicated in this situation

src.q: Should antibiotic-associated colitis occur, amoxicillin/clavulanic acid should immediately be discontinued, a physician be consulted and an appropriate therapy initiated.
Anti-peristaltic medicinal products are contraindicated in this situation.
Imodium must not be used when inhibition of peristalsis is to be avoided
